newsitem.title: EGYPT: Computer failure halts trade on Cairo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Computer failure halts trade on Cairo bourse.

text.p: The Cairo stock exchange came to a complete standstill on Sunday after the bourse computer system crashed and was only restored five minutes before the end of the session, brokers said.
Volume was a paltry 5.79 million pounds ($1.70 million) -- its lowest level since early May -- and the Capital Market Authority's overall index fell 0.06 percent to 234.06 points.
"The system was down most of the day. It slowed down to a point that orders took 30 minutes to be processed. Trading was very, very low," said broker Sherief Khalifa of Hermes EFG.

About 45 percent of the day's turnover came from a single transaction worth $760,000 in dollar-denominated shares of Misr Gulf Oil Processing. Brokers said one of the firm's shareholders was selling his equity to another.
Despite the system failure, bourse favourite Central and West Delta Flour Mills was the day's most active share but the stock ended unchanged at 53.5 pounds.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills came a close second, and shares rose 1.25 pounds to 48.00.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 359.15 points from Thursday's 359.31 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also fell to 162.68 from 162.79.
